editorial:
Imagine being told you are better than LeBron James when you are just a kid in high school. That is exactly where Lenny Cooke started. You get to see the wild ride of a guy who had the whole world expecting him to be a global superstar, but instead, he ended up far away from the NBA. The vibe here is raw and honest. It does not feel like a polished TV show; it feels like you are just hanging out with Lenny, listening to him talk about his regrets and his dreams while walking through his neighborhood.

What really works here is how the directors keep things moving. You feel the tension and the sadness of a man who is still trying to figure out where things went wrong. While it is a bit slow in some parts, the real-life drama keeps you interested. If you love sports stories that are not just about winning, you need to see this. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you are a movie collector, you might want to hunt down a physical copy to keep in your library.
endingExplained: By the end, you see that Lenny is still stuck in a cycle of hoping for a big break that will probably never come. There is no big happy ending or a sudden comeback story. Instead, it wraps up with a sad look at how hard it is to move past a peak that happened when you were seventeen. You leave the movie feeling for Lenny as he accepts his reality.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about fame and failure.
